title: Valid object-valued named input arrays are skipped instead of extended
reasoning: Nx namedInputs arrays can contain non-string input definitions as well as strings. The generator currently only appends nxrust's canonical Rust cache patterns when every existing item is a string; if a consumer has a valid array containing an object input, initGenerator logs a divergence warning and leaves the array unchanged. That means a valid cache input configuration can fail to receive required Rust patterns, causing generated Rust projects to miss source/workspace files in Nx cache invalidation. The included tests cover string arrays and non-array values, but not mixed valid arrays, so this regression path is not protected.
reproduction: Create nx.json with {"namedInputs":{"rustSources":["{projectRoot}/src/**/*.rs",{"env":"RUSTFLAGS"}]}} and run initGenerator({skipFormat:true}); the generator will not append missing RUST_SOURCES_PATTERNS entries and will warn instead.
recommendation: Treat any array-valued named input as mergeable, append missing string patterns while preserving existing object entries, and only warn for non-array or otherwise unsupported namedInputs values.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only exercise all-string arrays and a scalar string divergence case; they do not include a valid namedInputs array containing object entries.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where namedInputs.rustSources contains both a string and an object input, then assert missing Rust source patterns are appended and the existing object is preserved without a divergence warning.
minimumFixScope: Update mergeNamedInput in src/generators/init/generator.ts and add a focused initGenerator spec for mixed array named inputs.
